messages:
maya (customer): Hey team, hitting a weird failure with JSON mode in streaming responses. Our Python client using the SDK's streaming parser sometimes throws JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 482. It only happens with structured_output=true and when the model emits tool/metadata tokens. Repro steps below.

maya (customer): Repro (minimal):
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
resp = client.stream.generate(model='rwd-2.1', structured_output=True, prompt=my_prompt)
for chunk in resp:
    # our parser expects well-formed incremental JSON chunks
    parsed = chunk.structured  # sometimes raises json.JSONDecodeError
```

maya (customer): Stack: JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 482 (char 481)
maya (customer): We tried toggling max_tokens, switching models, still happens. Happens for ~1 in 200 requests.

carmen (support): Sorry you're hitting this, @maya. Can you paste the request_id or the full raw stream capture? Also which SDK version?

maya (customer): request_id=rid_01F4ZK8Q, SDK python v0.9.1, stream_transport=chunked. I attached a trimmed stream dump (private).

ben (sdk): Thanks @maya — this sounds like an incremental framing issue in the Python streaming JSON helper. Two quick asks: 1) can you reproduce with curl (raw streaming) to see if server frames are valid? 2) can you share the exact byte around char 480 (we suspect an unescaped control char or split UTF-8 boundary).

maya (customer): I did curl and saw the same truncated fragment around the same spot. The raw chunks show a backslash followed by newline split across chunks. Example around the failure: "notes":"Line1\\\nLine2\"" then next chunk continues "\", \"meta\": ...`. Parser tries to decode between chunks.

ben (sdk): Ah, looks like the SDK attempts to decode partial buffers when a complete JSON object hasn't closed. We added an aggressive incremental decode in 0.9.1 to lower latency, but it seems to mis-handle escaped sequences split across chunk boundaries (e.g., `\\n` split into `\\` + `n`).

dmitri (eng-runtime): Thanks for the signal — server-side doesn't alter escapes, we stream token-by-token. If a token boundary splits an escape sequence, client must buffer until a valid JSON token completes. But SDK should handle that. Ben, can you confirm where the decoder decides to call json.loads?

ben (sdk): Confirmed: in stream_parser.py we call _safe_decode(buffer) after every chunk. The heuristic was: try json.loads(buffer) and if it raises JSONDecodeError but not one indicating "Expecting value" at pos 0, we attempt incremental partial-emit. That heuristic was too permissive.

carmen (support): Temporary workaround for @maya — can you switch to non-streaming (fetch full response) or pin SDK to v0.9.0? Also set structured_output=False while we triage if that helps.

maya (customer): Non-streaming works fine. But streaming is critical for our use-case. Pinning to 0.9.0 is an option but we prefer a fix.

ben (sdk): We'll cut a patch to change the incremental decode logic: only attempt incremental parse when the buffer ends with a complete token boundary (heuristic: last char is `}` or `]`, or last 2 chars are `\"` with preceding escape check). Also add buffering for escapes split across chunks. I'll push a hotfix release v0.9.2 with tests.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: sdk-python-v0.9.2-hotfix -> canary (1/5)

ben (sdk): Patch pushed. Workaround: set client.stream_buffering='full' to disable aggressive incremental parsing in the meantime. Test case included: split escape sequences, multilingual UTF-8 split.

dmitri (eng-runtime): We'll also add a server-side test that avoids emitting splits in the middle of multi-byte UTF-8 sequences where possible, but long-term clients must be robust.

carmen (support): @maya, once canary finishes, can you try the new v0.9.2 and confirm?

maya (customer): Installing now, will test and report. Thanks. :pray:

maya (customer): Update: v0.9.2 resolved the issue in my test harness (5000 requests). No JSONDecodeErrors so far.

carmen (support): Great — marking this resolved. We'll include note in release notes: "Fix streaming parser handling of escaped sequences split across chunks (python v0.9.2)".

ben (sdk): Follow-up: added telemetry for these JSONDecodeErrors (counts + sample truncated bytes) and a regression test in CI. If anyone sees similar issues in TS/Go SDKs, please open issues.

carmen (support): Closing thread in 24h if no regressions from @maya. Thanks everyone! :tada:
